svg.title: German postwar atmospheric design branches
svg.desc: Six specialized German aircraft-development branches linked by radar, guided weapons, ground control, computing, and orbital warning. Exact service types and acceptance ordinals remain open.
svg.text: specialized mission schools · integrated combat system · exact post-1948 ordinals open

g.text: HIGH-SPEED INTERCEPTION
Messerschmitt design school
Me 262 and HG III research feed later interceptor projects.
Radar · guided weapons · propulsion integration · ordinal open
AIR SUPERIORITY
Focke-Wulf fighter school
Ta 183 bridges wartime work into postwar fighter projects.
Planform · handling · missile integration · ordinal open
THEATER STRIKE / RECONNAISSANCE
Arado fast-aircraft school
Ar 234 experience anchors fast strike and surveillance work.
Navigation · sensors · penetration · accepted types open
CLOSE SUPPORT
Dedicated battlefield-aircraft branch
Support requirements remain distinct from fighter procurement.
Survivability · control · low-level handling · types open
MARITIME / HEAVY AIRCRAFT
Junkers systems school
Research, long-range sensors, and heavy structures compound.
Endurance · communications · maritime weapons · types open
FLYING-WING FAMILIES
Horten-Gotha design school
Ho 229 and Horten XVIII sustain fighter, recon, and bomber work.
Pressure structures · penetration · strategic roles · codes open

svg.text: radar · guided weapons · ground control · computing · night and all-weather experience · orbital warning
The common system links specialized airframes; it does not restore the withdrawn 500-series fleet.
Design schools and mission structure are fixed; designations, dates, performance, weapons, production, and order of battle remain open.
